source_described_status.status_text: open theoretical exploration of interface-induced computation

provenance.supporting_text: This is an open theoretical exploration of interface-induced computation.

definitions.label: Task
definitions.content: A task is defined as a semantic invariant T=(X,Y,f), with f:X->Y independent of representation.

provenance.supporting_text: A task is defined as a semantic invariant ... f:X->Y ... is independent of representation.

definitions.label: Interface
definitions.content: An interface is rho=(tau,sigma), where tau transforms task structure into an executable dependency representation and sigma embeds that representation into a physical or symbolic layout.

provenance.supporting_text: An interface is a transformation rho=(tau,sigma) ... tau transforms task structure into an executable dependency representation ... sigma embeds that representation into a physical or symbolic layout.

definitions.label: Architecture
definitions.content: An architecture is a bounded resource vector A=(b1,...,bk), representing limits such as memory, bandwidth, attention, or storage.

provenance.supporting_text: An architecture is a bounded resource vector ... representing limits on computational resources such as memory, bandwidth, attention, or storage.

definitions.label: Executor
definitions.content: An executor resolves an admissible execution schedule pi in Pi_rho(T), where Pi_rho(T) is the set of execution schedules permitted by interface rho.

provenance.supporting_text: An executor resolves an admissible execution schedule ... where Pi_rho(T) represents all execution schedules permitted by interface rho.

formal_structures.label: Resource cost functional
formal_structures.content: C(rho,T)=inf_{pi in Pi_rho(T)} max_t v(pi,t); the source describes v(pi,t) as instantaneous resource utilization and the infimum as selecting the lowest peak-resource execution available under the interface.

provenance.supporting_text: The interface induces a resource-cost functional ... C(rho,T) = inf ... max_t v(pi,t) ... The infimum selects the lowest peak-resource execution available under the interface.

formal_structures.label: Reachability condition
formal_structures.content: A task is reachable when C(rho,T)<=A, with the inequality evaluated componentwise across resource dimensions.

provenance.supporting_text: A task is reachable when C(rho,T)<=A where the inequality is evaluated componentwise across resource dimensions.

assertions_or_hypotheses.content: A computational task is not intrinsically tractable or intractable; tractability is a relational property between a task, an interface, and an executing architecture.

provenance.supporting_text: A computational task is not intrinsically tractable or intractable; tractability is a relational property between a task, an interface, and an executing architecture.

assertions_or_hypotheses.content: Progress often occurs not by increasing raw computational capacity, but by discovering interfaces that transform problem structure into forms executable by bounded systems.

provenance.supporting_text: The central claim is that progress often occurs not by increasing raw computational capacity, but by discovering interfaces that transform problem structure into forms executable by bounded systems.

assertions_or_hypotheses.content: Progress in intelligent systems occurs through interfaces that transform task structures into forms whose peak computational demands fall within the resource limits of bounded architectures.

provenance.supporting_text: The framework hypothesizes that progress in intelligent systems occurs through interfaces that transform task structures into forms whose peak computational demands fall within the resource limits of bounded architectures.

limitations_or_open_questions.note: The README's open-theoretical-exploration statement is preserved separately as source-described status and is not rewritten into a specific open question.

Potential applications include: mathematical notation; programming languages; visualization systems; external cognitive tools; AI augmentation.
